parts.title: Risk taking
parts.article:
Risk taking

A We run risks. Most of the time we ignore them; sometimes we stop and decide how to deal with them. That’s life. Risks arise in sports, in business, in personal relationships; they are present in the laboratory, in political calculations, everywhere. Acting individually, we often prefer to gain some benefit by accepting some danger. Acting collectively, we make similar trade-offs.

B When society must assess risks, and those risks can be clarified, at least in part, by science, technology or mathematics, the responsibility of the research community is to be clear and complete. But that is not always so easy. Furthermore, too few people pay full attention to the best evidence, much less modify their behaviors as a result. Even when the evidence of high risk is clear – about smoking, for instance – many will deny the risk, or dispute it, or accept that it exists and still go ahead. As a former cigarette smoker, I understand denial.

C Perhaps more important than the basic facts of risk are the varied perception of it. Hearing the prediction of 60% chance of rain, or recognizing the minuscule likelihood of becoming ill from a flu shot, most people understand the right responses: take your umbrella and get your flu shot. But some, fearfully but irrationally, go to the extreme and stay at home and avoid all contact with other people. Irrational decisions occasionally affect us all. When it comes to risks the best odds do not always influence people to make the correct decision.

D In her book, The Universe and the Teacup, the science writer K. C. Cole reminds us that the risks of losing something and gaining something appear to be calculated in our minds according to quite different scales. People will risk a lot to prevent a loss, she notes; some people will rush into a burning building to save a pet. But they will usually risk very little if the only perceived outcome is a possible gain; many people won’t even risk pursuing an exciting job, if the current job, though unfulfilling, remains comfortable. That psychological mechanism, a desire to maintain the status quo, helps explain the high hurdles that any rational risk assessment must confront.

E Organizations face the same hurdles whenever they must cope with major shifts in policy. In his classic examination of the character of high-tech industry, Only the Paranoid Survive, Andrew S. Grove gives a perceptive account of a crisis that took place during his tenure as Chairman of the Intel Corporation. The business environment for Intel and its competitors was transformed by a flood of low-cost memory chips from Japan, and Intel made the difficult decision to abandon its chip-making business. Such a period of change in the outside world is filled with danger, Grove notes, precisely because it is so easy for executives to try to disregard it or misinterpret the mounting evidence showing the profound risks of not making change at the very core. The distinction Cole cites is instructive here: one reason management and staff may not act is that they tend to focus on the potential gains of risking change (which they characterize as small), rather than on the catastrophic losses that risking change could prevent. The period becomes critical for a company, according to Grove, and deadly when unattended to.

F Likewise, at the national level, and even the global one, institutions tend to be more willing to take a risk if it means avoiding a loss, than they are if it might confer a gain. Almost everyone, for instance, sees the signs of ecological decay. Reid J. Lifset’s article, ‘Full Accounting’, describes newly developed techniques for clarifying which critical decision would have the highest pay-offs for the environment. Once these ‘leverage points’ as he calls them, are located, many environmental organizations will be willing to risk the resources needed to prevent further deterioration.

G More complicated are decisions by nations to invest broadly in educational research. Some governmental leaders are oblivious to the risks posed by social underinvestment, because the urgent needs of the present take precedence over actions that would give rise to even more substantial gains in the future. Their attitude is that today’s risks must be manageable, and that tomorrow’s gains are at the very least difficult to measure. Better consideration and decision making for what lies ahead is essential.

H Nevertheless, I confess to being an optimist. My glass is generally half full – though that may not help me handle risk. Whether one’s temperament is optimistic or pessimistic, everyone in our scientific and engineering community has a social responsibility: measure with care and portray with honesty the level of risk involved in any action or decision.

questions.question: K. C. Cole points out that avoiding a loss seems more important to people than

analyses.content: 你可能会被“rush into a burning building”误导去选和紧急情况相关的选项，但这句话的核心对比是在“loss（损失）”和“gain（收益）”之间。

D段：People will risk a lot to prevent a loss, she notes; some people will rush into a burning building to save a pet. But they will usually risk very little if the only perceived outcome is a possible gain;
原文明确指出人们为了“避免损失（prevent a loss）”愿意冒很大风险，但如果只是为了“可能获得的收益（possible gain）”就不太愿意冒险，说明避免损失比获得收益（achieving a gain）更重要。

questions.question: According to Andrew S. Grove, it can be very dangerous for companies to ignore

analyses.content: Grove认为，当“外部世界发生变化（change in the outside world）”时充满了危险，因为高管们很容易去忽视（disregard）它，对应选项“外部发生的变化（changes occurring externally）”。
你可能想选和公司内部或现状相关的选项，但原文特别强调了危险来自无视“外部世界（outside world）”的变化。

E段：Such a period of change in the outside world is filled with danger, Grove notes, precisely because it is so easy for executives to try to disregard it or misinterpret the mounting evidence showing the profound risks of not making change at the very core.

questions.question: Reid J. Lifset argues that environmental agencies can benefit from

analyses.content: 原文说新开发的技术能查明哪些决策对环境回报最高（即最有效的解决方案），找到这些点后环保组织就能更好地投入资源去行动，对应“关于最有效解决方案的最新发现”。
你可能会看到环保就想乱猜，但让环保机构获益的根本是文中提到的“新开发的技术（newly developed techniques）”带来的关于如何高效决策的新发现。

F段：Reid J. Lifset’s article, ‘Full Accounting’, describes newly developed techniques for clarifying which critical decision would have the highest pay-offs for the environment. Once these ‘leverage points’ as he calls them, are located, many environmental organizations will be willing to risk the resources needed to prevent further deterioration.

questions.question: The writer suggests that government leaders need to focus more on

analyses.content: G段：Some governmental leaders are oblivious to the risks posed by social underinvestment, because the urgent needs of the present take precedence over actions that would give rise to even more substantial gains in the future. Their attitude is that today’s risks must be manageable, and that tomorrow’s gains are at the very least difficult to measure. Better consideration and decision making for what lies ahead is essential.
作者批评政府领导人只顾眼前的紧急需求，并在段末强有力地总结“对未来（what lies ahead）的事情进行更好的考量和决策是必不可少的”，完美对应“为未来做规划”。
你可能会看到原文说领导人关注“现在的紧急需求（urgent needs of the present）”就误选C（继续现状），但这恰恰是作者批评的短视行为，作者真正建议的是关注未来。

questions.question: the areas of study that help us understand risk

analyses.content: 这段话一开头就直接列举了“科学、技术或数学（science, technology or mathematics）”这些具体的研究学科领域，来帮助我们澄清和评估风险。
你可能在其他段落寻找“研究”这个词，但只有B段实实在在地给出了能帮助弄清风险的具体“学科（areas of study）”名称。
B段：When society must assess risks, and those risks can be clarified, at least in part, by science, technology or mathematics, the responsibility of the research community is to be clear and complete.

questions.question: reference to key actions that might benefit the world

analyses.content: 文中提到的能为环境带来最高回报的“关键决策（critical decision）”，正是对应了题干里能让世界受益的“关键行动（key actions）”。
你可能会因为“benefit”去寻找经济收益相关的段落，但这里的“世界”在原文中具体化为了“环境（environment）”的改善。
F段：Reid J. Lifset’s article, ‘Full Accounting’, describes newly developed techniques for clarifying which critical decision would have the highest pay-offs for the environment.

questions.question: examples of statistical predictions that the majority of the public react to in the same way

analyses.content: “60%降雨概率”和“极小的生病几率”就是统计预测的例子，而“大多数人（most people）”都会做出带伞和打疫苗的相同反应，对应了公众反应一致。
你可能会被后半段“极少数人躲在家里”误导，但题干问的是“大多数公众（majority of the public）”的统一反应例子，答案就在段落开头。

C段：Hearing the prediction of 60% chance of rain, or recognizing the minuscule likelihood of becoming ill from a flu shot, most people understand the right responses: take your umbrella and get your flu shot.

questions.question: the variety of contexts in which risk occurs

analyses.content: 你可能会把选项想得很复杂去找深奥的道理，但看到“everywhere”以及前面一连串的具体场景排比，就应该毫不犹豫地选A。
A段：Risks arise in sports, in business, in personal relationships; they are present in the laboratory, in political calculations, everywhere.
段落中用排比句一口气列举了体育、商业、人际关系、实验室和政治算计等多个场景，完美对应了风险出现的“多种情境（variety of contexts）”。

questions.question: mention of a habit that has been proved to be very risky

analyses.content: 文中直接点出“吸烟（smoking）”就是一个已经被证明有高风险的习惯，但很多人依然照做不误。
你可能一直在全文地毯式搜索“habit”这个词，但直接找到具体的危险行为“吸烟（smoking）”才是解题的关键。
B段：Even when the evidence of high risk is clear – about smoking, for instance – many will deny the risk, or dispute it, or accept that it exists and still go ahead.

questions.question: reference to market forces motivating change

analyses.content: 日本廉价芯片的大量涌入彻底改变了商业环境，迫使英特尔放弃原有的业务做出改变，这就是典型的“市场力量（market forces）”推动改变的例子。
你可能会被“change”误导去选政策变化的段落，但“市场力量”明确对应的是英特尔公司面临的“商业环境（business environment）”竞争。
E段：The business environment for Intel and its competitors was transformed by a flood of low-cost memory chips from Japan, and Intel made the difficult decision to abandon its chip-making business.

questions.question: the writer’s current attitude towards risk

analyses.content: H段：Nevertheless, I confess to being an optimist. My glass is generally half full – though that may not help me handle risk.
作者在段首直接坦白自己是一个“乐观主义者（optimist）”，看杯子总是半满的，这就是作者对自己面对风险时当前态度的直白陈述。
你可能会在第一段找作者的看法，但明确表达作者主观态度和自身性格（temperament）的只有最后一段的“I confess（我承认）”这里。

questions.question: a reason why some individuals avoid making a career change

analyses.content: 文中明确解释了人们不愿去追求新工作（逃避职业变动），是因为当前的工作虽然没成就感但很“舒适（comfortable）”，这是维持现状的心理机制在作祟。
你可能死死盯着“career change”这个词找，但原文的替换表达是“追求一份令人兴奋的工作（pursuing an exciting job）”，并详细给出了贪图舒适的理由。

D段：many people won’t even risk pursuing an exciting job, if the current job, though unfulfilling, remains comfortable. That psychological mechanism, a desire to maintain the status quo, helps explain the high hurdles that any rational risk assessment must confront.

questions.question: how some people over-react to information about risk

analyses.content: 面对极小概率的风险，有的人会因为恐惧“走向极端（go to the extreme）”，闭门不出并切断所有社交，这就是对风险信息的典型过度反应（over-react）。
你可能混淆了B段的“否认风险”，但“过度反应”对应的是把小风险无限放大的“走向极端”的行为。
C段：But some, fearfully but irrationally, go to the extreme and stay at home and avoid all contact with other people.

options.optionContent: risk is something we must try to avoid.

options.option: experts should be truthful about risk to the public.
options.optionContent: experts should be truthful about risk to the public.

options.option: optimists are better able to deal with risk than pessimists.
options.optionContent: optimists are better able to deal with risk than pessimists.

options.option: it is important to take risks in order to fulfil social obligations.
options.optionContent: it is important to take risks in order to fulfil social obligations.

questions.question: At the end of the passage the writer concludes that

analyses.content: 结尾作者明确总结，科学和工程界的专家们有社会责任去谨慎衡量并“诚实呈现（portray with honesty）”风险水平，完全对应B选项的“专家应该对公众如实说明风险”。
你可能会看到最后一段提到了“乐观者（optimists）”就急着选C，但作者开头第一句就排除了性格差异，强调无论乐观还是悲观，重点都在于“诚实说明风险”的社会责任上。

H段：Whether one’s temperament is optimistic or pessimistic, everyone in our scientific and engineering community has a social responsibility: measure with care and portray with honesty the level of risk involved in any action or decision.
